review_method.execution: No product, test, gate or engine execution for this review.

classification.EXTRACTED: Directly observable source operation, declaration or contract.
classification.INFERRED: Reasoned implication or limitation, explicitly separated from execution evidence.

review_method.definition_identity: name + start_line; nested definitions remain separate.
review_method.inventory_validation: Exact equality against root-provided independent AST definition ranges;92 definitions/90 names in this scope.
review_method.source_anchors: All anchors refer to the pinned ralphie.sh bytes, including explicitly cited cross-layer lines.

top_level.description: Bash entrypoint; ralphie-kernel marker identifies this product to shell-gate discovery. Header describes design intent rather than executable enforcement.

When not library mode and BASH_SOURCE is empty, reconstruct a header and consume remaining stdin into pwd/ralphie.sh.tmp.PID, chmod, rename to pwd/ralphie.sh and exec with RALPHIE_NO_UPDATE1. Failure removes scratch and exits1.
Enable errexit, nounset and pipefail before function definitions and normal execution.
Set VERSION3.1.0 and retain a literal newline in RALPHIE_NL rather than a stripped command substitution.
Layer1 defines output, portability shims and primitives shared by subsequent layers.
Derive physical script-parent SELF plus original basename ME. Initial PROJECT is nonempty RALPHIE_PROJECT or SELF parent; final CLI/environment binding occurs through project_bind later.
Use ANSI colors only on tty stdout with empty NO_COLOR and non-dumb TERM. VERBOSE and QUIET derive from RALPHIE_VERBOSE/RALPHIE_QUIET, each default0.
RUN_DEADLINE starts0, meaning unlimited. Header commentary says loop sets it, while current run_prepare actually starts it before preparation trials.
Layer2 introduces persistent state, append-only event writes, locking and process hygiene; STATE_KEYS declares the only writable state keys.
OWNS_RUN starts0; run_init changes it only after run setup begins.
One named directory list excludes generated/vendor/runtime paths from filesystem freshness evidence and is reused later by commit filtering.
LOCK_HELD starts0 and CHILD_PIDS starts empty. These are process-local cleanup bookkeeping, not durable process handles.
INTERRUPTED and SIGPIPE_SEEN start0. Traps are installed only later by install_traps.
Layer3 supplies deterministic stack inference, gate discovery/execution and Git operations; Git function bodies begin after the assigned boundary.
GATE_REAP installs an EXIT trap in the child gate shell that sends a default kill signal to jobs -p children.
Prefer executable BASH, then PATH bash. Both gate preludes enable pipefail. Last fallback is sh with no pipefail and GATE_NO_PIPEFAIL1.
GATE_EXEC_RC starts0 and is replaced by each gate executor result.
GATES_BASELINE_FILE starts empty and is bound to HOME_DIR/gates.baseline on first baseline operation.
GATES_SNAPSHOT starts empty; snapshot_gates grows it in the main process.
Lines1695–1696 are the Git subsection marker/blank line; git_ready starts1697 outside this inventory.

functions.name: project_bind
functions.summary: Resolve the selected project physically and bind every primary runtime path once.

inputs.description: Argument1 is an existing project directory; the caller may pass a relative path. Current working directory supplies relative-path interpretation.

outputs.description: Sets PROJECT, exported RALPHIE_PROJECT, HOME_DIR, STATE_FILE, EVENTS_FILE, GATES_FILE, OBJECTIVE_FILE, ASK_FILE, MEMORY_FILE, LOG_DIR, RUN_DIR, LOCK_FILE and STOP_FILE. No normal stdout.

side_effects.description: Exports the physical project path to child processes. The cd runs in command substitution; the caller working directory is unchanged. No directories are created here.

invariants.description: Every primary runtime path derives from the single physical PROJECT value.

failure_recovery.description: A failed directory resolution invokes die and exits1; it does not fall back to another project.

functions.name: terminal_printf
functions.summary: Print to stdout and translate a failed pipe write into the SIGPIPE cleanup protocol.

inputs.description: Printf format and arguments, plus /dev/stdout file type.

outputs.description: Formatted stdout; returns printf status, or141 when a failed write targets a pipe.

side_effects.description: On a pipe failure invokes on_pipe, which retires stdout and latches SIGPIPE_SEEN.

invariants.description: Only a failed write together with a pipe-shaped stdout takes the special SIGPIPE path.

failure_recovery.description: Ordinary non-pipe print failures retain their original status.

functions.name: say
functions.summary: Print one uncolored line through the pipe-aware output helper.

outputs.description: Stdout line and terminal_printf status.

side_effects.description: May trigger the shared broken-pipe protocol.

invariants.description: Formatting is fixed to %s followed by a newline.

failure_recovery.description: Print errors propagate through terminal_printf.

functions.name: info
functions.summary: Print an informational colored line unless quiet mode is true.

outputs.description: No output with successful status when quiet; otherwise formatted stdout.

side_effects.description: May trigger the shared broken-pipe protocol.

invariants.description: Suppressing a line succeeds because the guard uses OR.

failure_recovery.description: Print errors otherwise propagate through terminal_printf.

functions.name: good
functions.summary: Print a success-colored line.

inputs.description: Color globals and message arguments; QUIET is not consulted.

outputs.description: Formatted stdout and terminal_printf status.

side_effects.description: May trigger the shared broken-pipe protocol.

invariants.description: Success output remains visible in quiet mode.

failure_recovery.description: Print errors propagate through terminal_printf.

functions.name: err

outputs.description: Stderr line and printf status.

functions.name: dim
functions.summary: Print a dim line unless quiet mode is true.

inputs.description: QUIET, color globals and message arguments.

outputs.description: Successful silence when quiet; otherwise formatted stdout.

side_effects.description: May trigger the shared broken-pipe protocol.

invariants.description: Suppressing the message does not cause a false command failure.

failure_recovery.description: Print errors otherwise propagate through terminal_printf.

functions.name: dbg
functions.summary: Print a debug line to stderr only when verbosity is true.

inputs.description: VERBOSE, color globals and message arguments.

outputs.description: Optional stderr line; returns0.

side_effects.description: Direct stderr write when enabled.

invariants.description: The final OR true makes debug output non-fatal.

functions.name: die
functions.summary: Report a prefixed fatal message and exit.

outputs.description: Stderr via err, then process exit1.

failure_recovery.description: No local continuation after exit1.

invariants.description: Uses date +%s.

failure_recovery.description: Date failure has no local fallback.

outputs.description: YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ plus newline on stdout.

failure_recovery.description: Date failure has no local fallback.

functions.name: have
functions.summary: Check whether command resolution can find a name.

inputs.description: Argument1 command name and current shell/PATH command resolution.

outputs.description: Only command -v status; stdout and stderr are discarded.

side_effects.description: No invocation of the named command.

invariants.description: Presence is a resolution check, not a health or authentication probe.

failure_recovery.description: Missing names return nonzero.

functions.name: sha_of
functions.summary: Hash stdin using the first available supported digest tool.

inputs.description: Stdin bytes and availability of sha256sum, shasum and openssl.

outputs.description: Digest text; fallback is cksum checksum-bytecount.

side_effects.description: Runs one selected external digest implementation.

invariants.description: Selection order is sha256sum, shasum -a256, openssl SHA256, then cksum.

failure_recovery.description: No retry follows a present digest tool failing; fallback choice is based on presence. cksum is explicitly weaker than SHA256.

functions.name: timeout_cmd
functions.summary: Return the available GNU timeout command name or an empty line.

outputs.description: timeout, gtimeout, or an empty line.

side_effects.description: No timeout command is executed.

invariants.description: timeout is preferred over gtimeout.

failure_recovery.description: No available timeout produces a successful empty result.

functions.name: rand_token
functions.summary: Generate a small run/lock token.

inputs.description: Readable /dev/urandom, od presence, current time and shell PID.

outputs.description: Twelve hexadecimal characters when urandom is used; otherwise epoch seconds concatenated with PID.

side_effects.description: Reads6 random bytes or the system clock.

invariants.description: The fallback avoids relying on Bash RANDOM alone.

failure_recovery.description: No uniqueness or cryptographic guarantee follows from the fallback; od failure is not retried locally.

functions.name: json_escape
functions.summary: Escape textual stdin for a JSON string body.

outputs.description: Backslashes, quotes and tabs escaped; CR and other control bytes dropped; input line boundaries represented as literal backslash-n.

side_effects.description: Runs a sed/awk pipeline with C locale for sed.

invariants.description: It emits the string body without surrounding quotes or a trailing newline of its own.

failure_recovery.description: This deliberately is not binary-preserving JSON serialization. Pipeline failures have no local recovery.

functions.name: json_str
functions.summary: Escape a single argument as a JSON string body.

outputs.description: Escaped text on stdout.

side_effects.description: Pipes the argument to json_escape.

invariants.description: Printf prevents the argument from acting as a format string.

failure_recovery.description: Propagates pipeline failures.

functions.name: is_int
functions.summary: Recognize a nonempty unsigned decimal digit string.

outputs.description: Status0 for digits only;1 for empty or any other byte.

functions.name: is_true
functions.summary: Recognize common case-insensitive true values.

outputs.description: Status0 for1/true/yes/y/on;1 otherwise.

side_effects.description: Lowercases through tr.

invariants.description: False, empty and unrecognized spellings return1.

failure_recovery.description: No diagnostics for invalid values.

functions.name: trim
functions.summary: Trim leading and trailing whitespace from an argument.

outputs.description: Trimmed text on stdout.

side_effects.description: Runs sed.

invariants.description: Whitespace processing follows sed line semantics.

failure_recovery.description: No local recovery for a failed text pipeline.

functions.name: tail_of
functions.summary: Read a bounded tail of an existing regular file.

inputs.description: Argument1 path; optional byte count default4000.

outputs.description: Up to the requested trailing bytes on stdout; returns0.

side_effects.description: Reads the file, suppressing tail stderr.

invariants.description: Missing/nonregular files are a successful empty read.

failure_recovery.description: Tail failure is suppressed by OR true.

functions.name: secs_since
functions.summary: Compute elapsed seconds from an epoch value.

inputs.description: Optional epoch argument default0 and current system time.

outputs.description: Current epoch minus supplied integer, without newline.

side_effects.description: Reads the system clock.

invariants.description: A non-integer input is normalized to0.

functions.name: file_bytes
functions.summary: Return a regular file byte count or zero.

outputs.description: Unsigned decimal count, normalized to0 when absent, nonregular, failed or invalid.

side_effects.description: Reads file contents through wc -c.

invariants.description: Checks regular-file existence before opening the path.

failure_recovery.description: A failed count is replaced by0; concurrent path changes are not locked.

functions.name: count_of
functions.summary: Count stdout lines from an arbitrary supplied command.

inputs.description: All arguments form the callback command argv.

outputs.description: Nonnegative integer line count, or0 on pipeline failure/invalid count.

side_effects.description: Executes caller-supplied command; its stderr is suppressed and its stdout is consumed.

invariants.description: A nonzero callback status becomes count0 under inherited pipefail.

failure_recovery.description: No-match grep is normalized without creating a duplicated zero. Callback side effects are not constrained.

functions.name: human_secs
functions.summary: Format a duration in seconds, minutes or hours.

outputs.description: Ns, NmNs or NhNm without newline.

side_effects.description: None besides stdout.

invariants.description: Invalid integers normalize to0; hours output omits residual seconds.

failure_recovery.description: No handling beyond unsigned-digit validation.

functions.name: budget_left
functions.summary: Compute remaining time under the absolute run deadline.

outputs.description: -1 for unlimited; otherwise seconds remaining clamped at0.

side_effects.description: Reads the system clock.

invariants.description: Only a positive deadline creates a bounded budget.

failure_recovery.description: The global deadline is trusted numeric input here.

functions.name: budget_expired
functions.summary: Test whether an active run budget is exhausted.

outputs.description: Status0 exactly when budget_left is the string0.

side_effects.description: None beyond the clock read delegated to budget_left.

invariants.description: Unlimited (-1) does not count as expired.

failure_recovery.description: No local recovery beyond budget_left.

functions.name: budget_cap
functions.summary: Clamp a requested timeout to the remaining run budget.

outputs.description: Requested limit when unlimited; bounded minimum with a1-second floor otherwise.

side_effects.description: No persistent mutation.

invariants.description: Requested0 means no local limit; an exhausted finite budget still produces1 rather than unlimited0.

failure_recovery.description: Invalid requested integers normalize to0. The return is a timeout value, not a guarantee of exact wall-clock termination.

functions.name: state_get
functions.summary: Read the last stored value for a key, or a supplied default.

outputs.description: Last matching key=value suffix or default on stdout.

side_effects.description: Reads the state file using grep/tail.

invariants.description: Missing/nonregular state returns the default. Duplicate keys use the last line.

failure_recovery.description: The key is interpolated into a regex and is expected to be an internal key; read failures are suppressed.

functions.name: state_set
functions.summary: Replace one allowlisted state key using a directory mutex and temporary file.

inputs.description: Key/value arguments, STATE_KEYS, HOME_DIR, STATE_FILE; time/PID/randomness for scratch identity.

outputs.description: Best-effort state update; no success receipt other than file state. Unknown keys and unwritable HOME_DIR return0 after debug text.

side_effects.description: Creates HOME_DIR; may repair STATE_FILE; creates/removes state.lock; rewrites a same-directory temporary file and renames it; failure fallback removes state and writes the single requested key.

invariants.description: Only allowlisted keys are accepted; CR and LF are removed from values. The normal path verifies the rename destination is a regular file.

failure_recovery.description: After30 failed mutex acquisitions the lock is forcibly replaced. Rename/postcondition failure takes a best-effort destructive state fallback; preservation of other keys is not guaranteed by that fallback.

functions.name: state_bump
functions.summary: Increment a state counter through the common writer.

inputs.description: Key and optional increment default1; state value default0.

outputs.description: Updated state via state_set.

side_effects.description: Mutates one state key.

invariants.description: An invalid existing counter becomes0.

failure_recovery.description: Increment expression is trusted; state_set retains its best-effort semantics.

functions.name: event
functions.summary: Append one textual JSON event and update the last-write timestamp.

inputs.description: Kind/status/detail arguments and optional key=value extras; CY_N/RUN_ID_MEM globals, state fallback, paths.

outputs.description: One appended events.jsonl record with ts/run/cycle/kind/status/detail and string extras; state updated_at.

side_effects.description: Creates HOME_DIR, repairs a nonregular existing ledger path, appends bytes, then updates state.

invariants.description: In-memory run/cycle identities take precedence over editable state; detail and extra values pass through JSON escaping. Records are appended, not rewritten by this function.

failure_recovery.description: Kind/status/run/extra-key strings are trusted structural inputs rather than escaped values. File write failures have no independent durable queue or fsync.

functions.name: ensure_dirs
functions.summary: Create the three runtime directories on demand.

outputs.description: Returns0.

side_effects.description: mkdir -p may create project runtime directories.

invariants.description: Repeated calls are allowed.

failure_recovery.description: Creation failures and stderr are suppressed.

functions.name: ensure_own_file
functions.summary: Repair or report an unusable Ralphie-owned file without rejecting the caller.

inputs.description: Path, human-readable file type, GATES_FILE identity, CMD and UNUSABLE_REPORTED globals.

outputs.description: Returns0; refreshes GATES_FILE_BROKEN for the gate path; may update UNUSABLE_REPORTED.

side_effects.description: May chmod u+r; preserves readable read-only regular-file content; may recursively delete a nonusable existing path and create an empty file; emits console text and potentially one file-unusable event.

invariants.description: Readable protected regular files are not made writable or truncated. Repair success is reported only after replacement succeeds. The broken-file flag is gate-specific.

failure_recovery.description: A path failing -e, including a dangling symlink, returns early. Unrepairable gate paths set GATES_FILE_BROKEN1. Recursive deletion is actual behavior for nonusable existing paths; source comments do not prove their contained data is valueless.

functions.name: ensure_state_file
functions.summary: Apply common owned-file repair to the state path.

outputs.description: Returns ensure_own_file status, which is designed as0.

side_effects.description: May repair/report the state file.

invariants.description: Uses the shared repair policy.

failure_recovery.description: The wrapper does not reconstruct state counters; rebuild_state_from_ledger is a separate step.

functions.name: rebuild_state_from_ledger
functions.summary: Reconstruct cycle counters and cycle elapsed time from retained event generations.

inputs.description: EVENTS_FILE and numeric generations; RUN_DIR scratch path; state writer.

outputs.description: Restores max cycle, pass_count, fail_count and positive unverified/blocked/untrusted/learned/time totals; emits a rebuilt event and warning.

side_effects.description: Creates/deletes ledger-all.$$ scratch, rewrites selected state keys, appends one event.

invariants.description: Only cycle timing records contribute seconds; engine timing is excluded. Run-specific token and recovery identity values are not guessed.

failure_recovery.description: Concat failure falls back to the current ledger. No positive cycle causes cleanup/return. Reconstruction is limited to retained textual matching records, not a full JSON replay.

functions.name: ledger_init
functions.summary: Initialize/repair shared runtime storage without claiming ownership of a run.

outputs.description: Fills missing cycle/pass_count/fail_count/status/started_at defaults; may recover retained counters.

side_effects.description: Creates directories, repairs owned files, writes missing state, may append recovery events. Does not set OWNS_RUN or make pre-dirty snapshots.

invariants.description: Existing nonempty default keys are left unchanged. Rebuild occurs only for empty state with a nonempty current ledger.

failure_recovery.description: This initializer can mutate storage even for commands described as read-only in comments. Discover/help/version bypass it in main; general status does not. Repair/write helpers keep their own failure behavior.

functions.name: run_init
functions.summary: Start run-owned bookkeeping and remove stale per-PID scratch files.

inputs.description: RUN_DIR; timestamp/random token; caller-held run lock is an ordering precondition.

outputs.description: Sets RUN_ID_MEM and OWNS_RUN1; writes run_id, run_tokens0 and run_cost0.

side_effects.description: Deletes matching stale pre-dirty/staged/index/committed/commit-error artifacts; writes state.

invariants.description: Ownership is enabled only after run identity and usage reset are attempted. No snapshot is made here.

failure_recovery.description: Scratch deletion is best effort. Lock ownership is not checked inside this function; run_prepare supplies that ordering.

functions.name: ensure_ignored
functions.summary: Exclude Ralphie runtime storage using local Git exclusion metadata.

inputs.description: PROJECT, HOME_DIR/state, Git repository discovery and .git/info/exclude.

outputs.description: No machine stdout; optional debug message.

side_effects.description: May create Git info directory and append a comment plus .ralphie/ exclusion.

invariants.description: Does not edit the tracked .gitignore. An existing effective ignore rule avoids a duplicate append.

failure_recovery.description: No repository, failed metadata resolution/directory creation, or append failure is tolerated without aborting the caller.

functions.name: prune_artifacts
functions.summary: Prune old numbered cycle artifacts and then consider ledger rotation.

inputs.description: State cycle, RALPHIE_KEEP_CYCLES default50, LOG_DIR and RUN_DIR.

outputs.description: No normal stdout; delegates rotation result.

side_effects.description: Deletes old cycle log/answer/prompt and associated before/after gate captures.

invariants.description: Walks backward from cycle-minus-keep and stops at the first cycle missing all three primary artifacts.

failure_recovery.description: Invalid keep becomes50. Deletion errors are suppressed; gaps can stop pruning older leftovers.

functions.name: rotate_ledger
functions.summary: Rotate an oversized current ledger into bounded numbered generations.

inputs.description: EVENTS_FILE size, RALPHIE_LEDGER_MAX default16777216, RALPHIE_LEDGER_GENERATIONS default5.

outputs.description: Optional appended ledger-rotated event in a new current file; returns0 on normal/early paths.

side_effects.description: Renames .n-1 to .n from high to low, then current to.1. The highest retained generation may be overwritten.

invariants.description: Current records are moved as a file rather than rewritten record by record. keep and loop index are initialized separately to avoid Bash dynamic-scope declaration leakage.

failure_recovery.description: Failure moving the current ledger returns0. Rotation is finite retention rather than perpetual history. Retention environment values are not validated locally.

functions.name: prune_sessions
functions.summary: Delete oldest lexical session-directory entries beyond retention.

outputs.description: No normal stdout.

side_effects.description: Lists/sorts entries and recursively removes the first count-minus-keep names.

invariants.description: No session directory or no excess entries is an early return. Invalid keep becomes5.

failure_recovery.description: Deletion failures are suppressed. The line-based listing assumes generated session names, not arbitrary newline-containing paths.

functions.name: mark_tree
functions.summary: Touch the work-change timestamp marker.

outputs.description: Returns0.

side_effects.description: Creates RUN_DIR and truncates/creates tree.mark.

invariants.description: Marker path is owned runtime storage.

failure_recovery.description: Both mkdir and marker-write failure are suppressed.

functions.name: tree_listing_digest
functions.summary: Digest the sorted set of non-noise regular-file pathnames.

outputs.description: Hash text from the pathname listing.

side_effects.description: Walks the project filesystem; no file contents are hashed.

invariants.description: Every name in NOISE_DIRS is pruned by find; remaining regular-file pathnames are listed. The name predicate applies to any matching entry, not just directories.

failure_recovery.description: Failed cd produces an empty listing; find errors are suppressed. Newline-delimited names and the weak digest fallback limit this to a change heuristic.

functions.name: mark_verify
functions.summary: Record the current verification marker and file-set digest.

inputs.description: RUN_DIR and project filesystem through tree_listing_digest.

outputs.description: Sets LAST_VERIFY_LISTING.

side_effects.description: Creates/truncates verify.mark; creates RUN_DIR.

invariants.description: Both timestamp and pathname-set evidence are captured.

failure_recovery.description: Marker creation failure is suppressed; later missing-marker checks make the cache stale.

functions.name: verify_mark_stale
functions.summary: Tell callers whether filesystem evidence invalidates a cached verdict.

inputs.description: RUN_DIR/verify.mark, LAST_VERIFY_LISTING, current non-noise regular files.

outputs.description: Status0 for missing marker, a newer file, or changed pathname digest; nonzero otherwise.

side_effects.description: Filesystem reads only.

invariants.description: Deletion is observable through the listing digest even when find -newer cannot report it.

failure_recovery.description: This is timestamp/name-set evidence, not exhaustive content freshness or a concurrency barrier.

functions.name: find_changed_since
functions.summary: List regular project files newer than a supplied marker.

outputs.description: Newline-delimited find paths relative to project root.

side_effects.description: Filesystem metadata reads only.

invariants.description: Captures marker before replacing positional arguments with the find predicate. Every matching NOISE_DIRS name is pruned before regular-file testing.

failure_recovery.description: Failed cd exits the subshell successfully with no output; find errors are hidden.

functions.name: tree_touched
functions.summary: Check the work-change marker for any newer non-noise regular file.

outputs.description: Status0 if marker missing or a newer path exists;1 otherwise.

side_effects.description: Filesystem reads only.

invariants.description: Absence of the marker is treated as changed.

failure_recovery.description: Deletions alone are not detected by this function. Timestamp granularity remains a filesystem property.

functions.name: work_changed
functions.summary: Combine the Git/runtime fingerprint with filesystem modification evidence.

inputs.description: Before-fingerprint argument, current PROJECT/runtime state and tree.mark.

outputs.description: Status0 when fingerprint differs or tree_touched succeeds.

side_effects.description: Filesystem/Git reads through helpers.

invariants.description: Either signal is sufficient to report change.

failure_recovery.description: The check inherits the coverage limits of fingerprint and tree_touched; it is not a content snapshot.

functions.name: fingerprint
functions.summary: Digest Git-visible state together with gate and objective bytes.

outputs.description: Digest of HEAD/status/diff/gates/objective concatenated output.

side_effects.description: Runs Git reads and reads two runtime files.

invariants.description: Tracked content differences are included through git diff HEAD, not only status letters.

failure_recovery.description: Git/read errors are tolerated. It does not hash all untracked/ignored content; it must be combined with timestamp/listing signals for cache decisions.

functions.name: lock_acquire
functions.summary: Acquire the per-project run lock and reject an apparently live owner.

inputs.description: HOME_DIR, LOCK_FILE, process PID/time, existing pid/token/since files, process table.

outputs.description: LOCK_HELD1 on success; explicit1 on unwritable storage, live owner, acquisition failure or token race loss.

side_effects.description: Creates lock directory/metadata, waits for a possibly starting owner, may recursively remove stale lock, writes a fresh token.

invariants.description: Fresh acquisition uses atomic mkdir; stale takeover waits and compares a surviving random token. kill0 and ps both count as liveness evidence.

failure_recovery.description: No lock capability is provided by the OS beyond mkdir. PID reuse, filesystem concurrency and stale-takeover races are not ruled out by static reading.

functions.name: lock_release
functions.summary: Release the lock when this process records ownership.

outputs.description: Sets LOCK_HELD0 and returns0.

side_effects.description: Recursively removes LOCK_FILE when the flag is1.

invariants.description: The in-memory flag gates removal.

failure_recovery.description: Removal errors are suppressed; release does not recheck the stored token.

functions.name: track_pid
functions.summary: Add a child PID to the in-memory cleanup list.

outputs.description: Updated space-delimited CHILD_PIDS.

side_effects.description: In-memory mutation only.

invariants.description: PIDs are retained for later cleanup.

failure_recovery.description: No validation or deduplication of supplied PID.

functions.name: untrack_pid
functions.summary: Remove a child PID from the cleanup list.

outputs.description: Updated space-delimited CHILD_PIDS.

side_effects.description: Runs text filters and updates memory.

invariants.description: Exact whole-line matching removes the PID after space splitting.

functions.name: child_pids_of
functions.summary: Find direct children of a PID using available process tools.

inputs.description: Parent PID and pgrep availability/process table.

outputs.description: Child PIDs, one per line.

side_effects.description: Process-table reads.

invariants.description: pgrep -P is preferred; ps/awk is the fallback.

failure_recovery.description: Process-read errors yield no children through OR true. A changing process tree is not frozen.

functions.name: kill_tree
functions.summary: Recursively signal a process and its currently visible descendants.

outputs.description: Returns successful best-effort cleanup.

side_effects.description: Signals descendants before the supplied PID.

invariants.description: Child discovery precedes signalling the parent at each recursive level.

failure_recovery.description: Signal failures are suppressed; detached/reparented children may escape this traversal.

functions.name: terminate_tree
functions.summary: Snapshot descendants, send TERM, then send KILL after a grace period.

outputs.description: No normal stdout.

side_effects.description: Builds a PID list; signals process group and each captured PID with TERM, sleeps2, then KILLs group/list.

invariants.description: Descendants are enumerated before the root is terminated so immediate reparenting does not erase already found children.

failure_recovery.description: Kill errors are ignored. It does not wait/reap the process, freeze PID identity, or discover descendants created after the snapshot.

functions.name: reap_children
functions.summary: Terminate tracked children that still appear live.

outputs.description: Clears CHILD_PIDS.

side_effects.description: Runs terminate_tree for each PID passing kill0.

invariants.description: Cleanup walks the recorded list, then resets it.

failure_recovery.description: No wait is performed here. Processes failing kill0 are skipped.

functions.name: on_exit
functions.summary: Perform EXIT cleanup while preserving run/error bookkeeping and SIGPIPE status.

inputs.description: Original shell status, SIGPIPE_SEEN, OWNS_RUN, INTERRUPTED and state status.

outputs.description: May set state status error and append an exit event; explicit exit141 when SIGPIPE was seen.

side_effects.description: Records owned dirty paths if this is a run, reaps children, releases lock, may write state/events.

invariants.description: Non-run commands do not claim run ownership or rewrite run status. SIGPIPE overrides the observed code to141.

failure_recovery.description: Bookkeeping is best effort. EXIT traps do not run on SIGKILL or machine failure; this code is not a power-loss durability proof.

functions.name: on_int
functions.summary: Stop an interrupted run and exit with conventional interrupt status.

inputs.description: INT/TERM/HUP trap delivery, OWNS_RUN and tracked process state.

outputs.description: Sets INTERRUPTED1; owned run status stopped and interrupted event; exits130.

side_effects.description: Writes console/ledger/state, records owned work, reaps children and releases lock.

invariants.description: The human channel is not read; interruption uses automated cleanup.

failure_recovery.description: Best-effort cleanup precedes exit130 for all three registered signals, not signal-specific143/129.

functions.name: on_pipe
functions.summary: Retire a broken stdout pipe without exiting inside the signal trap.

outputs.description: Sets SIGPIPE_SEEN1; redirects future stdout to /dev/null.

side_effects.description: Changes file descriptor1 for the current shell.

invariants.description: Defers final exit141 to on_exit to avoid Bash3.2 buffered-write corruption described in the source.

failure_recovery.description: The redirect has no local fallback if it fails. After a successful redirect the function latches the flag without an immediate exit.

functions.name: install_traps
functions.summary: Register the shared exit, interrupt and pipe callbacks.

outputs.description: Installed EXIT, INT, TERM, HUP and PIPE handlers.

side_effects.description: Overwrites handlers for those signals/events.

invariants.description: EXIT and signal cleanup are centralized.

failure_recovery.description: Signal-delivery behavior remains controlled by Bash and the operating system.

functions.name: pkg_manager
functions.summary: Choose a JavaScript package manager from root lockfile presence.

outputs.description: bun, pnpm, yarn, or default npm.

side_effects.description: Filesystem existence checks only.

invariants.description: Priority is bun, pnpm, yarn, npm.

failure_recovery.description: No executable, lockfile validity or multi-workspace check is performed.

functions.name: has_npm_script
functions.summary: Check a root package script using an available JSON parser or a loose text fallback.

inputs.description: Script name, PROJECT/package.json, availability of node/python3.

outputs.description: Status0 for a truthy named script according to the selected parser, otherwise1 or grep status.

side_effects.description: Runs a short Node or Python parser; otherwise reads text through grep.

invariants.description: Parsers inspect scripts, while grep only proposes a likely key.

failure_recovery.description: A selected parser failure returns1 without trying the later parser; malformed JSON produces no diagnostic. Candidate execution occurs later in gate_trial.

functions.name: has_make_target
functions.summary: Look for an explicitly written Make target in root Makefiles.

outputs.description: grep status for an anchored target-name pattern.

side_effects.description: Reads Makefiles as text; does not run make.

invariants.description: Requires at least one regular Makefile path.

failure_recovery.description: Missing alternate file errors are hidden; this is text detection rather than Make syntax evaluation.

functions.name: py_runner
functions.summary: Choose a command prefix for a Python project tool.

inputs.description: Tool name, project .venv/venv executable paths, uv.lock and PATH.

outputs.description: Relative virtualenv tool path, uv run TOOL, global TOOL, or empty string.

side_effects.description: Existence/executability checks only.

invariants.description: Project virtualenv executables precede uv and global tools.

failure_recovery.description: No selected tool is run or health-checked here.

functions.name: detect_stack
functions.summary: Infer a space-separated stack tag list from root metadata.

inputs.description: Known manifest paths, *.tf/*.sh and .git directory presence under PROJECT.

outputs.description: Tags node/typescript/python/rust/go/maven/gradle/ruby/php/elixir/deno/cmake/docker/terraform/make/shell/git as applicable.

side_effects.description: Filesystem and glob checks.

invariants.description: Multiple stack tags can coexist; tag order is not declared significant.

failure_recovery.description: Root-only heuristics do not prove tool availability or project correctness. The git tag requires a directory even though Git worktrees can use a file.

functions.name: discover_candidates
functions.summary: Preview candidate gate text using subshell-local text-only manifest helpers.

inputs.description: PROJECT metadata and parent helper functions.

outputs.description: Candidate shell command lines; returns0 through OR true.

side_effects.description: Defines two helper overrides only inside this subshell; no gate commands are executed.

invariants.description: The local overrides prevent Node/Python package parsing during discovery preview and do not replace runtime helpers in the parent.

failure_recovery.description: Candidate-generation failure is suppressed for the preview.

functions.name: has_npm_script
functions.summary: Preview a possible package script through a readable-file text match.

outputs.description: Status0 on key-pattern match; nonzero otherwise.

side_effects.description: Reads package.json through grep only.

invariants.description: This definition exists inside discover_candidates and bypasses JSON parser execution.

failure_recovery.description: False-positive key matches are possible because this is a preview heuristic, not JSON validation.

functions.name: has_make_target
functions.summary: Preview a Make target while skipping absent or unreadable Makefiles.

outputs.description: Status0 on the first anchored match;1 if neither readable file matches.

side_effects.description: Reads text through grep only.

invariants.description: This definition is scoped to discover_candidates.

failure_recovery.description: Unreadable files are skipped without invocation or diagnostics.

functions.name: discover_git
functions.summary: Run the limited discovery Git query with selected execution/network side effects disabled.

inputs.description: Git argv, PROJECT and configured filter.*.(clean|process) keys.

outputs.description: Passes Git stdout/stderr/status to its caller.

side_effects.description: Reads Git config; runs Git with core.fsmonitor=false, core.untrackedCache=false, configured clean/process filters cleared, GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS0 and GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH1.

invariants.description: Overrides apply to this command, not global Git configuration or subsequent gates.

failure_recovery.description: This is source-level suppression of identified Git mechanisms, not a general sandbox or proof against every external filesystem/provider behavior.

functions.name: cmd_discover
functions.summary: Print a project discovery report without starting a run.

inputs.description: REST must be empty; PROJECT metadata, existing objective/gate files, engine table/presence.

outputs.description: Human-readable Git/stack/instruction/plan/objective/gate/candidate/engine report; failure if arguments or project directory invalid.

side_effects.description: Uses a subshell cd and reads local files/Git metadata; no ledger initializer, gate trial or engine liveness call occurs here.

invariants.description: Reports configured gates and candidate gates distinctly. Explicit text states engines are not checked for auth or health.

failure_recovery.description: An unreadable gate file is reported; arbitrary gate text is not executed. File/Git read errors are mostly suppressed and can limit the report.

functions.name: gate_candidates
functions.summary: Emit root-level candidate health commands for recognized project stacks.

inputs.description: Root manifests/lockfiles, Make targets, available Python runners and shell file markers.

outputs.description: Ordered newline-delimited command strings for package scripts, Python, Cargo, Go, Deno, Elixir, Ruby, Maven, Gradle, Composer, Terraform, Make and shell checks.

side_effects.description: Reads project metadata; global has_npm_script may invoke JSON parsers. It does not execute the emitted checks.

invariants.description: Shell filenames are expanded when the gate runs rather than interpolated into source text. Ralphie copies identified by the first40-line marker are omitted.

failure_recovery.description: Unsupported layouts and nested workspace members need explicit gates. Command presence/correctness is not guaranteed until trial/execution.

functions.name: gate_tool_names
functions.summary: Extract simple tool names used to recognize unavailable-candidate errors.

outputs.description: Basename of its first split word and third word for a second-word -m invocation; returns0.

side_effects.description: Uses unquoted shell splitting and pathname expansion of the input string.

invariants.description: Only invoked tool/module names are intended to classify absence messages.

failure_recovery.description: It is not a shell parser and cannot resolve general wrappers, quoting, compounds or dynamically selected commands.

functions.name: gate_exec
functions.summary: Execute one gate in the selected shell with capture, deadline and process cleanup.

inputs.description: Command, output-file path, optional hard seconds default0; PROJECT, GATE_SH and GATE_PRELUDE.

outputs.description: Merged stdout/stderr in the capture; return status stored in GATE_EXEC_RC.

side_effects.description: Enables job control to launch a background group, cd to project, exec shell -c, stdin /dev/null; tracks PID, waits via watchdog, then signals surviving process group/children.

invariants.description: The same executor is used by trial and measured gates. Idle timeout is0; the caller supplies hard timeout.

failure_recovery.description: Gate commands run with inherited operator permissions and can mutate arbitrary reachable state. Watchdog returns real rc or124 for timeout; cleanup is best effort and not an isolation boundary.

functions.name: gate_trial
functions.summary: Run a candidate and reject unavailable tools while retaining ordinary failing checks.

outputs.description: Returns2 for rc126/127 or a recognized absence line naming the invoked tool;0 otherwise.

side_effects.description: Creates/removes trial.$$ output and runs the candidate through gate_exec.

invariants.description: A runnable failing project check remains a candidate. Trial success means suitability, not a green project.

failure_recovery.description: The message/tool-name heuristic can misclassify complex commands. Timeout124 is not rejected by the explicit unavailable cases. The timeout_cmd result is assigned but unused.

functions.name: discover_gates
functions.summary: Discover and persist gate commands when no gate file exists or redetection is explicit.

inputs.description: Force argument default0; GATES_FILE/HOME_DIR, candidate metadata and trial environment.

outputs.description: Gate file with explanatory header, active commands and unavailable comments; gates-discovered event.

side_effects.description: May remove a dangling gate symlink, create runtime storage/temp file, execute every candidate trial, write through GATES_FILE and remove temp. No gate found records a nonblocking human question.

invariants.description: An existing regular gate file, including an empty one, is retained unless force1. Normal publication writes through the path to preserve supported symlinks.

failure_recovery.description: The cat-to-gates publication falls back to mv. Candidate execution is real project code, not a dry scan. Missing gates remain explicitly unverified.

functions.name: gates_list
functions.summary: List active configured gate command lines.

outputs.description: All lines excluding whitespace-only and leading-whitespace comments; returns0 for missing/outside/nonregular/unmatched input.

side_effects.description: Reads gate file only after containment.

invariants.description: A gate is one noncomment shell-command line; text is returned verbatim otherwise.

failure_recovery.description: Read errors are suppressed; broken readability is surfaced by ensure_gates_file/run_gates separately.

functions.name: gates_count
functions.summary: Count active configured gates safely.

outputs.description: Integer line count.

side_effects.description: Reads gate file through gates_list.

invariants.description: Empty lists become0 through the common counter.

failure_recovery.description: Shares gates_list containment and empty-result behavior.

functions.name: run_gates
functions.summary: Measure the configured gates and record bounded per-gate evidence.

inputs.description: Optional logbase default RUN_DIR/gates, phase default observe, GATE_TIMEOUT900, GATE_RETRIES1, GATE_LOG_MAX262144, current budget and gate file.

outputs.description: Return0 if no failed commands, including no-gate mode; GATES_NONE disambiguates no evidence. Writes logbase.summary and numbered logs; sets failure/flaky/timeout globals.

side_effects.description: Repairs gate file, runs every active command, retries failed checks once when GATE_RETRIES>0, appends flaky event, deletes retry captures and truncates oversized primary logs to tails.

invariants.description: An unreadable gate file returns1, not UNVERIFIED. Verify phase ignores run-budget clamping and does not forgive fail-then-pass; observe can forgive that flake. Every configured gate is measured rather than stopping at first failure.

failure_recovery.description: rc124 sets timeout metadata. GATE_RETRIES is only a boolean threshold for one retry, not a retry count. Timeout and log limits are assumed numeric here; log trimming is after execution and does not bound peak disk use. timeout_cmd is unused.

functions.name: ensure_gates_file
functions.summary: Check gate-path containment before applying owned-file repair.

outputs.description: Sets GATES_FILE_BROKEN1 and returns0 on unresolved/outside target; otherwise shared repair result.

side_effects.description: May warn or repair an in-project gate path.

invariants.description: No repair is attempted through a path rejected by containment.

failure_recovery.description: Unresolvable parent directories also count as broken. Caller must inspect the flag; rc0 alone is not readability proof.

functions.name: baseline_gates_load
functions.summary: Restore gate commands missing from the previous-run baseline.

outputs.description: Sets GATES_BASELINE_FILE; when missing entries exist sets GATES_SNAPSHOT; returns1 if ordered restore fails.

side_effects.description: May rewrite gate file, emits restore event/warning and queues a human review question.

invariants.description: Exact-line baseline membership persists between runs; intentional shrink needs explicit redetection to reset the baseline.

failure_recovery.description: Unreadable/missing baseline or no missing entries avoids restore. Failure is reported as could-NOT-be-restored and returns1; event kind/status remains gates/restored even for the failure-detail branch.

functions.name: baseline_gates_save
functions.summary: Persist the current active gate set as the cross-run baseline.

outputs.description: Baseline file content; returns0.

side_effects.description: Directly overwrites baseline file with current active lines.

invariants.description: Defaults the baseline path once when unset.

failure_recovery.description: Write/list errors are ignored; this is not an atomic or independently protected persistence transaction.

functions.name: snapshot_gates
functions.summary: Grow the in-memory run gate set and write a diagnostic snapshot.

outputs.description: GATES_SNAPSHOT monotonically accumulates exact command lines; run/gates.before mirrors it.

side_effects.description: Updates memory, creates runtime directory and writes snapshot file.

invariants.description: Current file additions are retained; missing previous lines are not removed from memory during the run.

failure_recovery.description: Disk snapshot write failures are tolerated because guard uses the in-memory copy. It does not validate command semantics or underlying test files.

functions.name: check_gates
functions.summary: Run the gate guard and preserve tamper evidence for the whole cycle.

outputs.description: Sets CY_GATE_TAMPER1 on guard failure and copies nonempty GATE_TAMPER to CY_TAMPER_NAME; returns0.

side_effects.description: May invoke gate restoration and event writes.

invariants.description: Later successful checks do not clear CY_GATE_TAMPER in this function.

failure_recovery.description: Always returns0 so callers must use the cycle flag to enforce outcomes.

functions.name: resolve_link
functions.summary: Follow a leaf symlink chain with a bounded hop count.

outputs.description: Resolved non-link path text without newline, or status1 if a symlink remains after16 hops.

side_effects.description: Filesystem reads only.

invariants.description: Relative link targets are interpreted relative to the current link dirname. Cycles cannot spin forever.

failure_recovery.description: It does not canonicalize parent components or require target existence. A surviving leaf link is rejected, including after readlink failure.

functions.name: gate_path_inside_project
functions.summary: Determine whether the physically resolved gate parent is inside the physical project root.

inputs.description: GATES_FILE, PROJECT and existing parent directories.

outputs.description: Status0 for contained target parent;1 for failed resolution/cd/empty result/outside root.

side_effects.description: Reads symlinks and directory metadata.

invariants.description: Both target parent and project root use pwd -P before the slash-delimited containment comparison.

failure_recovery.description: This is a point-in-time path check, not an atomic open or filesystem sandbox. Missing parent fails closed.

functions.name: restore_gate_order
functions.summary: Merge missing snapshot commands back into their original order while retaining current comments and additions.

inputs.description: GATES_SNAPSHOT, current writable GATES_FILE and project containment.

outputs.description: Return0 after successful rewrite with matching byte count;1 on rejected path/write failure.

side_effects.description: Creates restore.$$ and keep.$$ siblings, stores snapshot lines in dynamically named shell variables, writes through the gate path, deletes scratch files; failed publication attempts to restore the old bytes.

invariants.description: Requires a writable contained destination. Existing comments/blank lines/added gates are copied; missing remembered commands are inserted before the next remembered successor. Publication preserves the gate path inode/symlink.

failure_recovery.description: Backup restoration is best effort and validated publication compares length, not content hash. No concurrent writer lock or fsync is used. Dynamic _gsnap_N variables remain shell state.

functions.name: guard_gates
functions.summary: Detect missing remembered gate commands, restore them if possible, and flag the cycle as tampered.

inputs.description: GATES_SNAPSHOT, GATES_FILE, PROJECT and runtime paths.

outputs.description: GATE_TAMPER description or last missing command;0 with empty snapshot/no missing lines;1 whenever containment or remembered-command loss is detected.

side_effects.description: May recreate nonregular/unreadable gate file with rm-rf/truncate/chmod, invoke ordered restore and append tamper event.

invariants.description: Restoration does not turn the detected tamper into success. Added commands remain permitted. Exact remembered lines are the protected unit.

failure_recovery.description: An empty snapshot provides no prior-set protection. It does not prove that a surviving command or its transitive dependencies retained the same meaning. Repair failures still return1.

functions.name: gate_failure_brief
functions.summary: Format a bounded prompt-ready explanation of the first recorded gate failure.

inputs.description: GATE_FAIL_CMD, GATE_TIMED_OUT and seconds, GATE_FAIL_LOG, GATE_BRIEF_BYTES default3000.

outputs.description: Failure or timeout explanation plus optional failing log tail.

side_effects.description: Reads log only.

invariants.description: Timeout is described as an unknown result rather than assumed project defect.

failure_recovery.description: No failure command returns0 silently. The final file condition can return1 when no log exists; callers must not treat this formatter as a success predicate.

interfaces.description: Input environment RALPHIE_PROJECT defaults to script directory; project_bind turns the selected existing directory into an exported physical path. CWD matters for relative selection and streamed install.
Primary templates: PROJECT/.ralphie/{state,events.jsonl,gates,OBJECTIVE.md,ASK.md,MEMORY.md,log,run,lock,stop}. No HOME environment override is used for these paths.
Streaming reads the remaining script bytes from stdin and publishes pwd/ralphie.sh via pwd/ralphie.sh.tmp.PID; exec receives original argv and RALPHIE_NO_UPDATE1.
State is line-oriented key=value; last matching key wins. Values written by state_set have CR/LF removed. Only STATE_KEYS is writable through that function.
State writer uses STATE_FILE.lock as a mkdir mutex and STATE_FILE.tmp.PID.TOKEN as a rename scratch. After30 failed lock attempts it removes/recreates the mutex.
Append one compact JSON object per line with ts/run/cycle/kind/status/detail; extra argv key=value fields become string-valued properties. Only detail/extra values are escaped at this boundary.
EVENTS_FILE.1..N are rotated generations; RALPHIE_LEDGER_MAX default16777216 and RALPHIE_LEDGER_GENERATIONS default5 bound retained history. Max size/generation values are not locally validated.
Rebuild reads current plus EVENTS_FILE.[0-9]* into RUN_DIR/ledger-all.PID and extracts cycle/counter/timing values textually.
run_init clears pre-dirty.PID.nul, staged.PID.nul, index.PID, committed.PID.nul and commit-error.PID. Cycle retention RALPHIE_KEEP_CYCLES defaults50; session retention RALPHIE_KEEP_RUNS defaults5.
RUN_DIR/tree.mark and verify.mark plus LAST_VERIFY_LISTING combine modification times with a sorted regular-file name digest. NOISE_DIRS excludes runtime and build/cache/vendor trees.
Noise names are .git .ralphie node_modules .venv venv target dist build __pycache__ .next vendor .pytest_cache .mypy_cache .ruff_cache .tox coverage .nyc_output .terraform .gradle .idea .vscode.

Ordinary fingerprint invokes Git rev-parse HEAD, status --porcelain and diff HEAD, then includes gates and objective content. Unlike discover_git, these calls do not carry discovery-only config overrides.
ensure_ignored may append .ralphie/ into the repository metadata info/exclude resolved by Git, while leaving tracked .gitignore unchanged.
LOCK_FILE is a directory containing pid, token and since; live-owner checks use kill0 or ps. The token is checked after stale takeover, and LOCK_HELD controls later removal.
CHILD_PIDS is a space-delimited process-local list. pgrep-P or ps supplies children; cleanup sends TERM/KILL to PIDs and process groups. These are observations and signals, not process isolation.
EXIT calls on_exit; INT/TERM/HUP call on_int and exit130; PIPE calls on_pipe, retires stdout and causes final exit141. Owned-run exit cleanup records work and releases lock.

Stdout helpers use terminal_printf; warnings/errors/debug use stderr. RALPHIE_QUIET suppresses info/dim, RALPHIE_VERBOSE enables dbg, NO_COLOR/TERM/tty state control color. /dev/stdout determines pipe handling.
System date supplies UTC/epoch values, /dev/urandom plus od supplies tokens with epoch+PID fallback, and sha_of selects an available SHA256 tool or weaker cksum.
RUN_DEADLINE is absolute epoch seconds,0 unlimited. budget_cap floors finite expired limits to1. run_prepare sets the deadline from MAX_MINUTES before discovery and --gate trials.

Detection uses root package.json, tsconfig.json, pyproject.toml/setup.py/requirements.txt, Cargo.toml, go.mod, pom.xml, build.gradle(.kts), Gemfile, composer.json, mix.exs, deno.json, CMakeLists.txt, Dockerfile, Makefile/makefile and .tf/.sh glob presence.

Package-manager lockfiles select bun/pnpm/yarn/npm. Python tools prefer executable .venv/bin or venv/bin, then uv run with uv.lock, then global PATH. Normal package-script lookup optionally invokes node or python3.

Read-only discovery consumes standing-instruction filenames AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/GEMINI.md, known root plans and docs/TODO.md, current objective/gates, Git status and engine executable presence. It prints these facts and candidate text without running gates or engines.

discover_git applies GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS0/GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH1, disables fsmonitor/untracked-cache and configured clean/process filters for its Git invocation. It does not export these settings into later gate commands.
GATES_FILE is one shell command per nonblank/noncomment line, executed from PROJECT. Original active lines are protected by exact text membership; added lines remain allowed.

GATE_SH -c receives pipefail/EXIT-reap prelude plus command text. Stdin is /dev/null, stdout and stderr merge into the requested capture, command execution inherits operator authority and environment.
GATE_TRIAL_TIMEOUT defaults120 and GATE_TIMEOUT900. All gate execution delegates hard timing to watchdog_wait; verify is not clamped to the remaining run budget. Gate hard timeout returns124.

GATE_RETRIES defaults1 and enables one retry when positive. Observe may forgive failed-then-passed; verify does not. GATE_LOG_MAX defaults262144 retained bytes; GATE_BRIEF_BYTES defaults3000 prompt-tail bytes.

Execution writes RUN_DIR/trial.PID during trial, or logbase.summary plus logbase.N.log and temporary .retry/.trim files. Summary records PASS, FAIL(rc), UNVERIFIED or UNREADABLE. GATES_NONE must accompany rc0 to disambiguate absent checks.

run_gates resets/sets GATES_NONE, GATE_FAIL_CMD, GATE_FAIL_LOG, GATE_FLAKY, GATE_TIMED_OUT and GATE_TIMED_OUT_SECS; gate_exec records GATE_EXEC_RC. These values are consumed by later lifecycle/prompt decisions.

Persistent HOME_DIR/gates.baseline protects between-run command membership; in-memory GATES_SNAPSHOT and run/gates.before protect current-run membership. Restore uses GATES_FILE.restore.PID and .keep.PID.
Gate reads/repairs/resets in these helpers resolve up to16 leaf symlinks and physicalize the target parent/root before containment. This path check does not confine what a gate command can access.

Discovery with no gates or cross-run gate restoration calls ask_human; that later function writes deduplicated questions to ASK.md, confirms persistence, emits events and calls notify. It does not read a terminal.

relationships.description: main parses args/load_spec, handles help/version, then calls project_bind before discover or ledger work. Library mode calls project_bind directly at the file end.
main dispatches discover immediately after binding and exits, before request scanning, ledger_init, traps, update, run_prepare and loop.
discover_candidates locally replaces has_npm_script and has_make_target inside its subshell so gate_candidates uses text-only preview parsing without changing runtime definitions.
run_prepare acquires the run lock, establishes time budget and run state, then later prepares gates and restores the persistent baseline before first-cycle work.
event appends evidence and calls state_set(updated_at). Repair may call event, so the UNUSABLE_REPORTED latch prevents repeating the same unusable-path reporting path.
ledger_init and cycle_begin can recover selected counters from retained event generations; run identity/tokens are not reconstructed by rebuild_state_from_ledger.

EXIT and interrupt handlers record_owned_paths only for OWNS_RUN1, then terminate tracked children and release the lock. The called custody implementation excludes operator/sibling/runtime paths separately.

gate_candidates emits possibilities; gate_trial executes them to distinguish unavailable tools from runnable failure; discover_gates persists accepted lines; run_gates measures their pass/fail result.
Both gate_trial and run_gates use gate_exec. The executor tracks the process, calls watchdog_wait with idle0 and caller hard limit, then cleans remaining descendants.
run_gates returns0 with GATES_NONE1 when no gates exist; later lifecycle code must read that flag as well as return status to avoid promoting absent evidence.

cycle_begin snapshots gates before gates/engine can execute. check_gates latches tamper evidence; cycle_verify checks around measured gates and acceptance, so restore success cannot erase the cycle flag.
baseline_gates_load restores missing prior-run lines; snapshot_gates protects the in-memory set; baseline_gates_save persists the current set after a cycle only if CY_GATE_TAMPER is not1.
cache_verdict stores fingerprint plus mark_verify after recording. cycle_observe reuses a verdict only when fingerprint matches and verify_mark_stale is false; otherwise it runs gates.

cycle_verify fingerprints and marks before acceptance, then re-runs health gates if acceptance changed tracked/runtime fingerprint or timestamp/file-set evidence. A second mutation by health clears acceptance instead of looping indefinitely.
run_gates records first failing command/log and any timeout metadata; gate_failure_brief emits a bounded tail and distinguishes a killed check from a demonstrated code defect.
Because rotate_ledger retains finitely many generations, recovery can reconstruct only that retained history; append-only writing does not imply unbounded historical availability.

The guard protects the exact command lines remembered in GATES_SNAPSHOT. A retained command can still execute changed tests, dependencies or external services; source membership alone cannot establish semantic equivalence.

limitations.description: This is a static, every-line review of1–1696 at the pinned SHA256. It executes neither tests, project gates nor provider engines and establishes no live readiness or performance result.

Project gate shell text and commands, package tooling, Git hooks/filters outside discover_git, provider implementations and external services can have behavior unavailable from this source. The runner is orchestration, not a sandbox.

Historical incident comments and design slogans document intent. The inventory describes executable operations separately; it does not independently reproduce those incidents or adopt absolute comments as proofs.
mkdir/rename/append and best-effort repairs provide source-level recovery mechanisms, but no fsync protocol, filesystem fault model or concurrent-writer proof is present in these functions.
Event rotation has finite retention. State rebuild derives counters/time from matching retained text and cannot reconstruct every prior state key or deleted history.

Fingerprint, mtimes and a newline-delimited regular-file list are complementary heuristics; they do not atomically snapshot all content or cover excluded directories, symlink targets and arbitrary external state.

ensure_own_file and guard_gates can recursively remove existing unusable paths. Readable protected regular files are preserved, but comment claims that directories contain no valuable data are not established by the code.

The script enables set-eu/pipefail. Bash errexit propagation depends on calling context, particularly conditionals; function descriptions record explicit returns/guards rather than claiming every failed subprocess always aborts or always recovers.
Watchdog hard limits include polling/grace overhead. run_gates trims captured output after a gate finishes, so retained-size limits alone do not bound peak disk consumption during execution.
Gate-path checks physicalize parents and reject unresolved leaf links, but no descriptor-based atomic containment or concurrent-renaming protection is shown here.

PID/process-group signals and descendant snapshots are best-effort cleanup. They cannot prove cleanup after SIGKILL/power loss or capture every child that reparents or changes session between observations.
A nonshrinking list of command strings constrains one edit surface; correctness still depends on the chosen commands and their implementations. Zero-gate rc0 requires the separate GATES_NONE flag.

Git custody, engine behavior, objective/acceptance logic, human notifications and most CLI behavior are inventoried by other reviewers. Only specifically cited cross-layer functions were read here to establish outgoing contracts.
